findings.summary: The takeaway ('on long high-rate loans it can exceed $200') and the $30,000 / 9% / 72-month feasibility case ($227.82) sit on a term exceeding 61 months, where 15 U.S.C. 1615(b) requires a refund at least as favorable as actuarial for precomputed consumer credit consummated after 9/30/1993. Presenting it as a typical lender outcome contradicts the page's own legality section.
findings.fix: In writing, label any term over 61 months as a formula illustration (a federally restricted term for precomputed consumer loans), prefer a 60-month example for the 'larger gap' case ($25,000 / 8% / 60 / 12 = $88.13, engine-computed), and make the calculator show a visible notice whenever term > 61 months. Keep the figures engine-computed, never hand-typed.

findings.summary: The legal claim must carry its full scope in the first answer, FAQ and takeaway: 15 U.S.C. 1615(b) applies to precomputed consumer credit transactions (not business loans) with a term exceeding 61 months consummated after September 30, 1993; it does not say the Rule of 78 is legal at 61 months or less (state law and contract can differ; source silence is not proof of legality). 1615(a) (prompt refund of unearned interest on full prepayment, under $1 exempt) applies regardless of term.
findings.fix: Writer closed fact list uses the exact subsection (b) wording above; never write 'illegal' or 'banned' without the over-61-month and precomputed-consumer conditions; do not assert any state-law position; tell readers to check the contract and request a payoff statement (1615(c): within 5 days, one free per year). Phase 4 tests this consequential claim against the 61-month counterexample.

findings.summary: Calculator and copy limits: model assumes level-payment, whole-month, fixed-rate precomputed loan with no fees or rebate-on-default, and the refund at payment k is computed from remaining finance charge; real contracts add fees and payoff-date conventions. Planned title 'Rule of 78 Calculator: Payoff Refund vs Actuarial' is a colon-spliced two-clause form against the headline rule (50 chars, length ok).
findings.fix: State assumptions and the method note beside the result with visible 'In our internal modeling, we compared ...' attribution and no tested/tested-and-reviewed wording; engine unit tests must cover k=n (difference 0), k=0 or invalid input, APR=0, term 1, and a golden case ($15,000/7%/48/12 -> Rule 78 earned $971.99, actuarial $943.34, difference $28.65); Phase 4 replays the engine. Prefer a non-spliced SEO title of 50-60 chars such as 'Rule of 78 Calculator for Loan Payoff Refunds' (45) extended to 50-60, keeping the primary keyword first; disclaimer at the page bottom only; no 'honest/actually' wording.
